'''Mikata Shrine''' (みかたじんじゃ) is a shrine located in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}} {{ill|Shisō, Hyōgo|Q877216|qid=Q877216}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=minor Shikinaisha}}, and its {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking}} was prefectural shrine.

It enshrines Ashiharashikoo no Kami ({{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}}), whose exploits are described in the "{{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|Q11498726|qid=Q11498726}}."

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
*Honden (main hall)
:The only nationally designated {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|de|Wichtiges Kulturgut Japans|es|Bien Cultural Importante de Japón|fi|Japanin tärkeä kulttuuriomaisuus|fr|Bien culturel important|id|Properti Kebudayaan Penting (Jepang)|it|Bene culturale importante (Giappone)|ja|重要文化財|ko|일본의 중요문화재|ro|Patrimoniu cultural important al Japoniei|simple|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|th|ทรัพย์สินทางวัฒนธรรมที่สำคัญ (ญี่ปุ่น)|tr|Önemli Kültürel Varlık (Japonya)|uk|Важливі культурні пам'ятки Японії|zh|重要文化財|qid=Q1188622}} structure in {{ill|Shisō, Hyōgo|Q877216|qid=Q877216}}.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|author= |year= |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/147621 |title=文化遺産データベース「御形神社本殿」 |publisher=文化庁 |accessdate=2015-12-06}}</ref> Built in the late {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, in Daiei 7 ({{ill|1527|Q6412|qid=Q6412}}). Three-bay nagare-zukuri style with cypress bark roofing. It is significant as an example of medieval shrine architecture whose construction date is clearly known. It was designated as a national Important Cultural Property on {{ill|June 15|Q2613|qid=Q2613}}, {{ill|1967|Q2648|qid=Q2648}} (Shōwa 42). Dismantling and restoration repairs were carried out in {{ill|1971|Q2475|qid=Q2475}}--{{ill|1972|Q2476|qid=Q2476}} (Shōwa 46--47), which revived the carvings and delicate bracket complexes from the time of the original late {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}} construction.

=== Shisō City designated cultural property ===
*Hyakunin Isshu illustrated picture votive tablets (ema)
:There are 17 ema panels in total. Examples depicting all one hundred poets are rare nationwide, and these are the only such examples in the prefecture. They are in good condition and can be regarded as extremely valuable surviving artifacts. Two inscriptions of provenance are attached, from which it is known that they were dedicated in Kōka 3 ({{ill|1864|Q7704|qid=Q7704}}).
